toegepas.rede_vinder: The pronoun refers to the plural veins (are/lyne), so 'hulle' makes the reference clearer than 'dit'.
toegepas.fout: 'dit' after a plural antecedent (die are, lyne) could also be read as pointing to 'die groen'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'hulle' points plainly to the veins that act as lines, with the same meaning.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Regte' is the natural everyday word for a Grade 4 learner; 'werklike' is stiff.
toegepas.fout: 'werklike' is stiff for a Grade 4 reader.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'regte klip' is the plain everyday word with the same meaning.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Iets aanraak' is the natural Afrikaans for touching something; 'aan hulle raak' is awkward.
toegepas.fout: 'aan hulle raak' for two things is awkward; Afrikaans says 'daaraan raak' or 'hulle aanraak'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'as jy hulle aanraak' is the natural verb with the same meaning.

toegepas.blok: Hoe om te kyk en te beskryf
toegepas.rede_vinder: A lesson does not own names; 'die name uit hierdie les' says more naturally that the learner uses the terms taught here.
toegepas.fout: 'hierdie les se name' reads as names the lesson owns rather than the terms it teaches.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'die name uit hierdie les' says plainly that the learner uses the terms taught here, with no change in meaning.

laat_vaar.voor: Hierdie kunselemente is reeds buite in die natuur self te sien.
laat_vaar.na: Jy kan hierdie kunselemente reeds buite in die natuur sien.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The passive 'is ... te sien' with 'buite' and 'self' stacked is wooden for Grade 4; an active sentence reads more naturally with the same meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'is ... te sien' is idiomatic Afrikaans, and the proposal drops 'self', which carries the contrast with art made by an artist in the sentence before.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Preposition: you see lines 'op' a leaf, matching 'op 'n foto'; 'aan' sounds unnatural with 'raaksien'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'aan die blaar self' is natural Afrikaans for a feature on the actual object, so the preposition swap is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.voor: Die ou blaar aan 'n tak kan diep groen wees en die nuwe een geel-groen.
laat_vaar.na: Aan 'n tak kan die ou blaar diep groen wees en die nuwe blaar geel-groen.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Putting 'aan 'n tak' first makes clear both leaves are on the branch, and 'die nuwe blaar' avoids the English-style prop word 'een'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The original already reads clearly; the reorder and the repeated 'blaar' only read differently.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Net 'n klein deel' is the idiomatic form; 'een' adds a counting sense the sentence does not need.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'een klein deel' deliberately echoes the definition's 'een deel van 'n ding' in the next sentence, so the change is lateral and loosens that link.

laat_vaar.blok: Hoe om te kyk en te beskryf
laat_vaar.voor: is daar 'n paar dinge om na te soek
laat_vaar.na: is daar 'n paar dinge waarna jy kan soek
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Dinge om na te soek' copies English 'things to look for'; a relative clause with 'waarna' is the Afrikaans construction.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'dinge om na te soek' is acceptable Afrikaans, and 'waarna jy kan soek' weakens the directive sense to a mere possibility.

vlae.rede: The title writes one colour apart ('ligte groen') and the other as a compound ('donkergroen'); 'liggroen tot donkergroen' or 'ligte groen tot donker groen' would be consistent. The title cannot be changed by this step, so it is flagged for the writer or a person.
